comment: What happens when an app reaches for a native module, checked by scripts/audit_modules.py.
`asked` is how React Native's own JavaScript asks for it: `get` answers null and `getEnforcing` throws.
`answeredBy` is who provides it here: `basalt` for this repository, `react-native` for ReactCxxPlatform or the shared defaults, `nobody` for the rest.
`effect` is what an app sees when nobody answers, which is the whole reason this file exists.
`hostSpecific` marks a module each desktop implements itself, so the three provider chains are allowed to differ about it.

`conditional` says when a module is answered rather than whether, and names the condition: a host offers Skia, Reanimated and worklets only when the build was pointed at an app that has the library, and React Native offers three of its own behind a feature flag, a debug macro or a dev UI delegate. The running-host check in e2e/turbomodules.tsx skips them, because a build without the condition answers null and is right to -- and the three upstream ones are the reason that check exists at all: the provider chains do not say when.

ActionSheetManager.effect: ActionSheetIOS throws when called: its module is nil and the first call reaches a method on it. A desktop app wants a menu or a dialog instead, which basalt-core has.

CPUTimeCxx.effect: Nothing an app reaches: Fantom is React Native's own test runner.

DevLoadingView.conditional: only when the host supplies a dev UI delegate, which it does with a dev server and not in a plain run

DevMenu.effect: Importing `DevMenu` from react-native throws, which is what made `export * from 'react-native'` unusable in basalt-core -- see the note in website/docs/reference/api.mdx. This platform has its own dev menu; see core/DevMenu.h.

DeviceEventManager.effect: Nothing: it is Android's hardware back button, and BackHandler resolves to the platform file rather than to this module off Android.

DialogManagerAndroid.effect: Nothing: it is Android's half of `Alert`, and `Alert.js` uses `AlertManager` off Android, which is answered here.

FrameRateLogger.effect: Nothing an app reaches: an internal performance logger.

ImageEditingManager.effect: `ImageEditor.cropImage` throws. No desktop equivalent is written yet, and cropping an image is a Skia or a Core Graphics call rather than a module.

IntentAndroid.effect: Nothing: it is Android's half of `Linking`, and `Linking.js` uses `LinkingManager` off Android, which is answered here.

JSCHeapCapture.effect: Nothing: a JavaScriptCore debugging hook, and this platform runs Hermes.

KeyboardObserver.effect: Nothing, and deliberately: `Keyboard.js` passes null for the module off iOS, so listeners are registered and never fire. A desktop has no soft keyboard to report.

ModalManager.effect: Nothing: `Modal.js` only reaches it on iOS, where it is the dismissal hook. A <Modal> here is a real window; see core/ControlMetrics.h.

NativeAnimatedTurboModule.effect: Nothing: `NativeAnimatedHelper` prefers `NativeAnimatedModule`, which React Native's own defaults answer, so `useNativeDriver` works.

NativeFantomCxx.effect: Nothing an app reaches: Fantom is React Native's own test runner.

NativeFantomTestSpecificMethodsCxx.effect: Nothing an app reaches: Fantom is React Native's own test runner.

NativeViewTransitionCxx.conditional: only when ReactNativeFeatureFlags::viewTransitionEnabled(), which is off by default

PushNotificationManager.effect: `PushNotificationIOS` throws. Local notifications are a package here instead; see packages/basalt-notifications.

ReactDevToolsRuntimeSettingsModule.conditional: only in a build with REACT_NATIVE_DEBUGGER_ENABLED_DEVONLY defined

ReactDevToolsSettingsManager.effect: DevTools settings are not persisted between runs. The runtime settings module beside it *is* answered, so the DevTools connection itself works.

RedBox.effect: Nothing: the legacy red box. LogBox is answered, and it is what React Native uses.

SampleTurboModule.effect: Nothing an app reaches: React Native's own example module.

SegmentFetcher.effect: Nothing an app reaches unless it uses RAM bundles with segments, which Metro does not produce here: one bundle per app.

SettingsManager.effect: `Settings.get` and `Settings.set` throw. iOS's user defaults have no desktop equivalent written yet; an app wants AsyncStorage or a file.

SoundManager.effect: No click sound from a Touchable, which is iOS's keyboard-click API.

Timing.effect: Nothing: the legacy timer module. Timers come from the runtime scheduler in the new architecture, so setTimeout and setInterval work.

UIManager.effect: Nothing, and this one is worth reading twice: `UIManager.js` resolves to `BridgelessUIManager` because `RN$Bridgeless` is true here -- ReactInstance.cpp sets it unconditionally -- so the legacy module is never asked for. A library that calls a method BridgelessUIManager does not implement gets its own error naming the method.

BasaltApp.what: This project's own: the app's identity and paths. See core/AppIdentity.h.

BasaltDialog.what: This project's own: the native file dialogs, which React Native has no API for. See core/DialogModule.h.

BasaltMenu.what: This project's own: the application menu, which on macOS is also what makes Cmd-C reach a field. See core/MenuModule.h.

BasaltWindow.what: This project's own: the host window a surface is in. Host-specific, each desktop having its own window object.

BasaltWindows.what: This project's own: more than one window, which is more than one surface. See core/WindowHost.h.

RNCSafeAreaContext.what: react-native-safe-area-context's module, answered so the library works unmodified. See core/SafeAreaComponent.h.

RNGestureHandlerModule.what: react-native-gesture-handler's module, answered whether or not the app has the library: it costs a name comparison.

RNSModule.what: react-native-screens' module, which basalt-navigation is built on. See core/ScreensComponent.h.

RNSkiaModule.what: react-native-skia's module, which installs Skia's whole JavaScript API. Host-specific: each desktop has its own canvas.
RNSkiaModule.conditional: only when the build was pointed at an app with @shopify/react-native-skia, behind BASALT_HAS_SKIA

ReanimatedModule.what: react-native-reanimated's module, when the build was pointed at an app that has it. See core/ReanimatedModule.h.
ReanimatedModule.conditional: only when the build was pointed at an app with react-native-reanimated, behind BASALT_HAS_REANIMATED

WorkletsModule.what: react-native-worklets' module, which Reanimated is built on. See core/WorkletsModule.h.
WorkletsModule.conditional: only when the build was pointed at an app with react-native-worklets, behind BASALT_HAS_WORKLETS
